claims.text: Machine learning-based logistic regression predicts new-onset diabetes within 5 years for hospitalized patients with an AUC of 0.78.
Machine learning models using administrative health data predict diabetes onset within 5 years with an AUC of 0.80.
Support vector machine classifiers utilizing facial texture features achieve 99.02% accuracy in detecting diabetes mellitus.
Deep learning models detect type 2 diabetes from fundus images alone or combined with clinical metadata with AUROCs ranging from 0.85 to 0.93.
The Guardian Connect System predicts hypoglycemic attacks 30 minutes in advance with an alert accuracy of 98.5%.

evidence.description: Choi et al. reported that the area under the curve (AUC) of predicting new-onset diabetes within 5 years for hospitalized patients was 0.78, derived from ML-based logistic regression.
Ravaut et al. recently reported that an ML model using administrative health data could predict diabetes onset within 5 years with an AUC of 0.80.
Shu et al. demonstrated that the best texture feature extractor for diabetes mellitus detection could achieve an accuracy of 99.02% using support vector machine.
Zhang et al. demonstrated that DL models could be used to detect T2D solely from fundus images or in combination with clinical metadata with AUROCs of 0.85–0.93.
According to product data for the Guardian Connect System, the accuracy of the alert was 98.5% 30 minutes before the onset of hypoglycemia.

methodologies.name: AI-assisted digital health-care ecosystem framework
methodologies.description: A comprehensive conceptual framework integrating AI algorithms with patient-reported outcomes, electronic health records, and clinical workflows across four stages: risk prediction, screening, basic management, and complication monitoring.

methodologies.name: Narrative review and synthesis
methodologies.description: A systematic overview and evaluation of artificial intelligence and machine learning applications in clinical diabetes research and management.

limitations.text: Rule-based clinical decision-support systems are expensive to build, brittle, and constrained by the comprehensiveness of pre-existing medical knowledge.
Self-reporting of food intake by patients in dietary monitoring is inaccurate and often impractical.
AI models trained on unbalanced or unrepresentative health data can amplify implicit bias and healthcare disparities.
Large language models in healthcare carry inherent risks of output inconsistency and generating misleading information.

future_work.text: Train AI algorithms on fair datasets that represent social, environmental, and economic factors to ensure algorithmic fairness.
Conduct prospective clinical trials to evaluate the real-world performance, safety, and workflow integration of AI systems in clinical practice.
Implement privacy-preserving decentralized learning architectures, such as swarm learning or federated learning, to protect sensitive medical data.
